Governor Kehoe's Statement Following Detonation at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant

November 25, 2026

Jefferson City

Following this morning's controlled, mitigated detonation of the lead azide stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, Governor Mike Kehoe acknowledged the actions taken by the State of Missouri since learning of the planned federal operation.
At this time, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) 
reports
 no detectable traces of lead heading towards Missouri.
“While the decision and responsibility of conducting this operation rested with the federal government, our state agencies remained focused on ensuring Missouri was prepared," said 
Governor Kehoe. "
I am grateful for the dedication of our state team members in planning for and responding to this event. From the beginning, we have worked to get answers for Missourians, ensure our state agencies have the resources necessary to respond, and keep the public informed.”
Governor Kehoe and state officials maintained communication with the White House, the U.S. Army, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 7, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and Iowa officials.
The Missouri National Guard also provided technical expertise to assist state agencies in assessing potential impacts to Missouri.
While there are no detectable traces of lead heading to Missouri and no anticipated impact to air, water, agriculture, and public health, state officials will continue to evaluate post-detonation findings and provide relevant information to Missourians as it becomes available.
Constituents looking for updated information, health guidance, and links to resources from state and federal agencies should visit the 
Missouri Department of Natural Resources' webpage
.
Statements from Cabinet Leadership:
“Thankfully, today’s lead azide detonation in Iowa was much less significant than we were prepared for,” said 
Missouri Department of Natural Resources Director Jake Buxton
. “We will continue working with our partners to monitor the situation and stand ready to respond appropriately if it becomes necessary.”
“We have been in close contact with our local public health partners in northeastern Missouri since becoming aware of the potential public health concerns,” said 
Department of Health and Senior Services Director Sarah Willson
. “We are grateful that, while our experts and partners quickly mobilized and prepared for potential impacts, air monitoring results now confirm that Missouri experienced the best-case outcome from this event.”
“Following the events in Iowa this morning, Missouri agriculture and the state’s food supply remain safe,” said 
Missouri Department of Agriculture Director Chris Chinn
. “As we head into this holiday season, we are thankful for the diligence of Missouri’s farmers and ranchers, who provide safe, nutritious, and delicious products for consumers here and around the world.”
“The projected impacts in Missouri were initially minimal, and we’re glad to hear that the post-detonation results show that any of those preliminary forecasted impacts are now obsolete in our state,” said 
Missouri Department of Public Safety Director Mark James
. “The State Emergency Management Agency will continue coordinating among state agencies as we monitor incoming winter weather accumulation and related hazards on one of the busiest travel days of the year.”
